subproblem.title: A linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U) with zeroth-order bounds on every compact subset of U is a current
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, and let L : 𝒟ⁿ(U) → ℝ be ℝ-linear (L : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ). Suppose that for every compact K ⊆ U there is c ∈ ℝ such that |L(ω)| ≤ c·M for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ K and every M ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ M for all x ∈ ℝ^P (‖·‖ the operator norm on n-covectors). Then there is a current S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n, i.e. L together with Simon's sequential continuity) with S(ω) = L(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (L : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ (ω : TestFormOn U n) (M : ℝ), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ K → (∀ x, ‖(ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x‖ ≤ M) → |L ω| ≤ c * M) → ∃ S : GeometricCurrentOn U n, ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, S ω = L ω
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof of cmcs_restrict_current (sequential continuity), with the integral functional S₀ replaced by an arbitrary linear functional L satisfying the zeroth-order estimate that step 4 uses for S₀.

For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) write ω̂ := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) for its underlying form, and ‖·‖ for the operator norm of n-covectors.

1. (Reduction.) A GeometricCurrentOn U n is a structure ⟨T₀, h⟩ consisting of a linear map T₀ : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ and a proof h that T₀(ω_j) → 0 for every sequence (ω_j) with TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0; its value S(ω) is T₀(ω). Take T₀ := L. Then S(ω) = L(ω) holds by definition for every ω, and it remains to prove: if (ω_j)_{j∈ℕ} in 𝒟ⁿ(U) satisfies TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0, then L(ω_j) → 0 in ℝ.

2. (Unpacking the convergence.) By definition of TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0 there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω̂_j ⊆ K for all j such that, for every k ∈ ℕ, iteratedFDeriv ℝ k ω̂_j → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k 0̂ uniformly on K, where 0̂ is the underlying form of the zero test form, i.e. the zero function. Apply the hypothesis to this compact K ⊆ U to obtain c ∈ ℝ with |L(ω)| ≤ c·M whenever ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω̂ ⊆ K and ‖ω̂(x)‖ ≤ M for all x.

3. (Zeroth-order smallness on K.) For every function G and point x, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 G x‖ = ‖G(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero). In particular ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0̂ x‖ = ‖0̂(x)‖ = 0, so iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0̂ x = 0 for every x. Uniform convergence for k = 0, in metric form (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff together with eventually_atTop), says: for every η > 0 there is N such that dist(iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0̂ x, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω̂_j x) < η for all j ≥ N and all x ∈ K. This distance equals dist(0, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω̂_j x) = ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω̂_j x‖ = ‖ω̂_j(x)‖ (dist_zero_left). Hence ‖ω̂_j(x)‖ < η for all j ≥ N and all x ∈ K.

4. (Off K.) If x ∉ K, then x ∉ tsupport ω̂_j (because tsupport ω̂_j ⊆ K), so ω̂_j(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and ‖ω̂_j(x)‖ = 0 ≤ η. With step 3: for every j ≥ N, ‖ω̂_j(x)‖ ≤ η for all x ∈ ℝ^P.

5. (Conclusion.) Let δ > 0 and put η := δ/(|c| + 1) > 0; let N be as in step 3 for this η. For j ≥ N, the hypothesis applied to ω := ω_j and M := η (valid by tsupport ω̂_j ⊆ K and step 4) gives
   |L(ω_j) − 0| = |L(ω_j)| ≤ c·η ≤ |c|·η = δ·|c|/(|c| + 1) < δ,
   using c ≤ |c|, η ≥ 0, δ > 0 and |c| < |c| + 1. Since δ > 0 was arbitrary, L(ω_j) → 0 (Metric.tendsto_atTop). This is the continuity requirement, so S := ⟨L, h⟩ is a GeometricCurrentOn U n with S(ω) = L(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). ∎
proof_key_steps: Take S := ⟨L, h⟩; then S(ω) = L(ω) by definition, so only L(ω_j) → 0 for TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0 must be shown.
TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0 gives a compact K ⊆ U containing every tsupport ω_j and uniform convergence on K of the order-0 derivatives; take the constant c for this K.
‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 G x‖ = ‖G(x)‖ and the limit form is 0, so for every η > 0 eventually ‖ω_j(x)‖ < η on K; off K, ω_j(x) = 0.
With η = δ/(|c|+1): eventually |L(ω_j)| ≤ c·η ≤ |c|·η < δ, hence L(ω_j) → 0.

audit.reason: The proposition exactly matches the stated compact-support bound and the frozen current structure. Zeroth-order uniform convergence gives small norms on K, while support containment gives zero values outside K. Choosing η = δ/(|c|+1) proves sequential continuity without assuming c ≥ 0. Packaging L yields the stated evaluation identity. No sibling or parent theorem is used.

subproblem.title: Integrability and sup-norm bound for the pairing integral ∫_E ξ(ω) dμ of a form vanishing off a finite-measure set
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on ℝ^P (Euclid P), and let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n: continuous linear functionals on n-covectors) be μ-a.e. strongly measurable and such that, for μ-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| holds for every n-covector α, where |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α is the Euclidean coefficient norm. Let E, K ⊆ ℝ^P with K measurable and μ(K) < ∞, let ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) be continuous with ω(x) = 0 for every x ∉ K, and let ε ∈ ℝ satisfy |ω(x)| ≤ ε for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Then x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) is integrable with respect to μ restricted to E, and |∫_E ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x)| ≤ ε·μ(K), where μ(K) is read as the real number (μ K).toReal.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n) (E K : Set (Euclid P)) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (ε : ℝ), AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → Continuous ω → MeasurableSet K → μ K < ∞ → (∀ x, x ∉ K → ω x = 0) → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x) ≤ ε) → Integrable (fun x => ξ x (ω x)) (μ.restrict E) ∧ |∫ x in E, ξ x (ω x) ∂μ| ≤ ε * (μ K).toReal
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2 and 4 of the parent proof of cmcs_restrict_current (integrability of F_ω and the estimate |∫ F_ω dν| ≤ (pointwise bound)·ν(K) ≤ (pointwise bound)·μ(K)), stated for one continuous form ω that vanishes off a measurable set K of finite μ-measure, with the pointwise bound on ω expressed in the coefficient norm |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm (so the norm comparison of step 1 is not used here).

Notation. F(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)) ∈ ℝ; ν := μ.restrict E, so that ∫_E G dμ = ∫ G dν by definition of the set integral; g := K.indicator (fun _ => ε), i.e. g(x) = ε for x ∈ K and g(x) = 0 for x ∉ K.

1. (ε ≥ 0.) covectorEuclideanNorm is a square root, hence nonnegative (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg). Therefore 0 ≤ |ω(0)| ≤ ε by the hypothesis on ω at the point 0.

2. (Measurability of F.) The evaluation map ev : MultiVector P n × Covector (Euclid P) n → ℝ, ev(Λ, α) := Λ(α), is a bounded bilinear map (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply), hence continuous. ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable by hypothesis, and ω is continuous, hence μ-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable; ℝ^P is second countable). Therefore F(x) = ev(ξ(x), ω(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂ applied to g := fun Λ α => Λ α, whose uncurried form is ev).

3. (Pointwise domination.) By hypothesis there is a μ-conull set of points x at which |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| holds for every n-covector α. Fix such an x.
   - If x ∈ K: taking α := ω(x), ‖F(x)‖ = |ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ ε = g(x).
   - If x ∉ K: ω(x) = 0 by hypothesis, so F(x) = ξ(x)(0) = 0 because ξ(x) is linear (map_zero); hence ‖F(x)‖ = 0 = g(x).
   Thus ‖F(x)‖ ≤ g(x) for μ-a.e. x.

4. (The dominating function is integrable.) μ(K) < ∞, i.e. μ(K) ≠ ∞, so the constant function ε is integrable on K with respect to μ (integrableOn_const). Since K is measurable, the indicator g = K.indicator (fun _ => ε) is μ-integrable (IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator).

5. (Integrability of F.) By steps 2–4 and domination (Integrable.mono'), F is μ-integrable. Integrability is preserved by restricting the measure (Integrable.restrict), so F is ν-integrable, i.e. x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) is integrable for μ.restrict E. This is the first conclusion; no measurability of E is needed.

6. (Bound on the integral.) g is ν-integrable (Integrable.restrict applied to step 4), and ‖F(x)‖ ≤ g(x) for ν-a.e. x, because every μ-a.e. property holds (μ.restrict E)-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae applied to step 3). Hence, by norm_integral_le_of_norm_le,
   |∫_E F dμ| = ‖∫ F dν‖ ≤ ∫ g dν = ν.real(K)·ε,
   where the last equality is integral_indicator_const (K measurable) and ν.real(K) = (ν(K)).toReal.

7. (Comparison of measures; conclusion.) Since K is measurable, ν(K) = μ(K ∩ E) (Measure.restrict_apply) ≤ μ(K) (measure_mono, as K ∩ E ⊆ K), and μ(K) < ∞; hence (ν(K)).toReal ≤ (μ(K)).toReal (ENNReal.toReal_mono). Multiplying by ε ≥ 0 (step 1) and combining with step 6,
   |∫_E ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x)| ≤ ε·(ν(K)).toReal ≤ ε·(μ(K)).toReal.
   This is the second conclusion. ∎
proof_key_steps: ε ≥ 0, since the coefficient norm is nonnegative and |ω(0)| ≤ ε.
F(x) = ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable: the continuous evaluation map (Λ, α) ↦ Λ(α) composed with the a.e. strongly measurable ξ and the continuous ω.
For μ-a.e. x, |F(x)| ≤ ε·1_K(x): on K by the hypothesis on ξ applied to α = ω(x) and the bound on ω; off K because ω(x) = 0 and ξ(x) is linear.
ε·1_K is μ-integrable (K measurable, μ(K) < ∞), so F is μ-integrable by domination and hence μ⌞E-integrable.
|∫_E F dμ| ≤ ∫ ε·1_K d(μ⌞E) = ε·μ(K ∩ E) ≤ ε·μ(K), using ε ≥ 0.

audit.reason: All hypotheses and both conclusions match exactly. The proof derives ε ≥ 0, establishes measurable evaluation and integrable indicator domination, then restricts the measure. Measurability of K suffices for the indicator integral and restriction formula; E need not be measurable. Finite μ(K) justifies the toReal comparison. The proof is complete and independent of the other children.
